bull_case: AI-first ARR can turn the current disruption narrative into a new monetization cycle while buybacks shrink the share base.
bear_case: A permanent shift to model-native creation tools could compress ARR growth and terminal multiples.
thesis: Asymmetry is favorable because the downside case is close to current price while Base/Bull provide substantial upside. The key is that Adobe is not financially fragile; the debate is around moat duration and growth, not survival.

evidence.claim: Q3 AI-first ARR grew more than 150% y/y.
Adobe had more than 1B MAU across creativity and productivity.
Q2/H1 subscription revenue and ARR remained double-digit growth.

counterevidence: AI lowers content-creation barriers and could shift value from application vendors toward models, distribution layers or new agentic workflows.
unknowns: Long-run AI monetization per user, Firefly inference economics, and how much AI-first ARR is incremental versus bundled/reclassified ARR.
falsifiers: If ARR growth falls to low single digits while AI usage rises, or owner FCF/share stops compounding despite buybacks, the moat/compounder thesis is downgraded.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 파산 또는 영구손실 확률이 기대수익에 비해 지나치게 높음
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Recurring revenue, strong OCF and investment-grade scale make bankruptcy/permanent impairment unlikely relative to upside.
